definitions.gloss: lapis lazuli blue; deep azure; ultramarine blue
definitions.explanation: A vivid, deep blue color reminiscent of the gemstone lapis lazuli. One of Japan's traditional color names, evoking a rich, jewel-like blue.

examples.japanese: {瑠璃色|るりいろ}の{空|そら}が{広|ひろ}がっていた。
examples.english: A deep azure sky stretched out before us.

examples.japanese: {海|うみ}は{瑠璃色|るりいろ}に{輝|かがや}いていた。
examples.english: The sea was shining in a deep lapis blue.

examples.japanese: {瑠璃色|るりいろ}のガラスの{器|うつわ}をお{土産|みやげ}に{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a lapis blue glass vessel as a souvenir.

notes:
Composed of {瑠璃|るり} (lapis lazuli, a precious blue stone) and {色|いろ} (color). One of Japan's traditional color names ({伝統色|でんとうしょく}), carrying a sense of elegance and depth that plain "blue" does not convey. Frequently used in literary and poetic descriptions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {瑠璃色|るりいろ}の{空|そら}: deep blue sky
- {瑠璃色|るりいろ}の{海|うみ}: deep blue sea
- {瑠璃色|るりいろ}に{光|ひか}る: to gleam in lapis blue

CULTURAL NOTE:
{瑠璃|るり} is one of the Seven Treasures ({七宝|しっぽう}) in Buddhism, and the color has spiritual associations. The {瑠璃光|るりこう}{如来|にょらい} (Medicine Buddha) is associated with this color. The Japanese bird オオルリ (blue-and-white flycatcher) also takes its name from this color.

SIMILAR COLORS:
- {藍色|あいいろ}: indigo — darker and greener
- {紺色|こんいろ}: navy blue — darker and more subdued
- {群青色|ぐんじょういろ}: ultramarine — very similar, also derived from mineral pigments
- {青色|あおいろ}: blue — the general color name
